Belarus to Send Poorly Performing Farmers to Guard Ukraine Border — Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko said underperforming harvest workers – and officials – should be sent to the army to guard the Ukraine border as Minsk rallied for a bountiful harvest season. Fire Erupts Near Russia’s Largest Steel Plant After Reported Drone Attack in Lipetsk — A fire broke out near Russia’s largest steel producer, Novolipetsk Steel, in Lipetsk after residents reported explosions and a possible drone attack overnight. Russian officials confirmed a fire at industrial facilities but did not acknowledge an attack, while Ukraine has not commented.

Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty amid a deepening crisis in the country’s defense leadership. IMF Approves $690 million for War-Torn Ukraine After Review — The International Monetary Fund’s board completed a review of Ukraine’s financing arrangement, clearing the way for immediate access to about $690 million, the Fund said on Monday.

Former SBU Special Forces Chief Takes Over Ukraine’s Defense Ministry Amid Fedorov Fallout — Former SBU Special Forces chief Yevhen Khmara took over as Ukraine’s acting defense minister on July 20 following President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to appoint him to the role. The move comes as protests continue over the dismissal of reformist Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Sanctioning Russia is Popular in America — A bipartisan survey shows overwhelming US support for tougher measures against Russia, with strong backing for sanctions, actions against officials involved in abducting Ukrainian children, and penalties on foreign companies doing business with Moscow. Majorities across Republicans, Democrats, and independents also favor expanding US–Ukraine defense cooperation.

Zelensky Faces Deepening Political Crisis as Protests Dig In — President Volodymyr Zelensky faces mounting political pressure as protests over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov enter a fifth day.
